events.headline: Nasdaq 100 posts its worst day since June as chipmakers drop nearly 7%, driven by renewed AI-capex/debt concerns after Meta signaled higher spending plans
Oil extends gains (WTI near $98-99, Brent near $111) on Saudi-Iran supply worries as Middle East tensions persist and US crude inventories fall more than expected
10-year Treasury yield falls to ~4.95% as markets price in roughly 80% odds the Fed holds rates at the Oct 28 FOMC meeting; Chair Warsh has declined to pre-commit

Security firm Lava reports finding Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs tied to IP addresses linked to China Telecom, raising export-control compliance questions (unconfirmed whether chips are physically in China; Nvidia says it follows export rules)
